Russian Missiles Kill 3, Injure 15 in Kyiv, Disrupts Power Supply — Russian ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv on Nov. 20 killed three people and injured 15 others. The attacks damaged three bridges and critical infrastructure, disrupted traffic and triggered emergency power outages across several districts.

Shoigu’s Ex-Deputy Jailed for 10 Years Over $80M Military Procurement Scandal — A Moscow court sentenced former Russian First Deputy Defense Minister Ruslan Tsalikov, a longtime Sergei Shoigu ally, to 10 years in a high-security penal colony for embezzlement, money laundering, and bribery. He was also fined 500 million rubles and ordered to repay the defense ministry more than 6.5 billion rubles. A separate organized-crime charge was dismissed, and his lawyers said they would appeal.

Europe Calls for Winter Ceasefire, Reaffirms Postwar Troop Plans Despite Putin’s Threats — European leaders urged Russia to halt winter attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure while reaffirming plans for a multinational force despite Putin’s threats. They also called for a Black Sea ceasefire, legally binding security guarantees and European participation in peace negotiations.
Russian Drone Hits Kharkiv Hospital, Injuring 5 — A Russian drone struck a hospital in Kharkiv, injuring 5 people and damaging more than 50 windows, according to Mayor Ihor Terekhov.

Russia Hits 3 Kyiv Bridges in Overnight Ballistic Attack — Russian ballistic missile strikes damaged Kyiv’s Podilsko-Voskresenskyi, Darnytskyi and South bridges early Friday, Nov. 20, prompting traffic restrictions as fires broke out across the capital.

Macron Calls to Reopen Ukraine’s NATO Membership Bid in Response to Russia’s Demands — French President Emmanuel Macron called for renewed discussions on Ukraine’s NATO membership, citing Russia’s maximalist demands and Ukraine’s growing military strength. Speaking after the Berlin summit, he urged immediate air defense support and backed European involvement in peace negotiations.

‘We Won’t Allow It Again’: Merz Says Europe Will Not Accept ‘Yalta 2’ — German Chancellor Friedrich Merz rejected a new Yalta-style division of Europe, presenting Berlin summit leaders with pieces of the Berlin Wall as a warning against repeating history. His remarks followed the Trump-Putin-Xi summit, whose peace declaration omitted Ukraine.

Kushner Says Trump Wants Europe ‘By His Side’ on Ukraine — US envoy Jared Kushner said President Donald Trump wants Europe involved in any Ukraine peace agreement rather than imposing a unilateral settlement. Following Berlin talks, Kushner said he and Steve Witkoff conveyed European leaders’ strong and united support for Ukraine to Trump, while signaling progress on NATO-style security guarantees.

UK Pledges to Stand With Ukraine ‘For as Long as It Takes,’ Burnham Says in Berlin — At the Coalition of the Willing summit in Berlin, Burnham said Europe was ready for peace negotiations but would discuss wider European security with Moscow only after Ukraine and Russia reached a peace agreement.

Japan’s PM Takaichi Holds First Talks With Putin Since 2022 — During a roughly 30-minute meeting at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen on Wednesday, Nov. 18, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi pressed Russian President Vladimir Putin to free detained Hokkaido Shimbun reporter Yuki Imai. The talks, the first between the countries’ leaders since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, also covered Japan Tobacco’s Russian businesses.

NovaPay Completes Acquisition of BTA Bank, Rebrands to NovaBank — Ukrainian logistics group Nova, via its subsidiary NovaPay Invest, has finalized the acquisition of BTA Bank to launch NovaBank. Following NBU approval on Nov. 12, the integration will combine NovaPay's technology with a banking license to expand digital and physical financial services for businesses and individuals.

Polish FM Slams Elon Musk for ‘Mouthing Russian Propaganda’ Over Ukraine History — Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski urged Elon Musk to stop “mouthing Russian propaganda” after the SpaceX CEO falsely claimed at The New York Times DealBook Summit that the US staged a coup in Ukraine in 2014. Musk was likely referring to the Maidan protests, a grassroots movement the Kremlin has framed as Western-backed. Musk also accused Zelensky of lying about Starshield disruptions and claimed Ukraine’s

Trump Open to NATO-Style Guarantee for Ukraine, Kushner Says — Senior US envoy Jared Kushner said on Thursday, Nov. 19, that US President Donald Trump is open to extending Ukraine a security guarantee modeled on NATO’s Article 5 mutual defense clause, provided it serves US interests and forms part of a broader security package. Speaking in Berlin after the Coalition of the Willing summit, Kushner claimed Russia had become comfortable with the concept, while stressing that any deal must be monito

Trump Questions Ukraine Aid in Unscheduled Call to European Allies — US President Donald Trump questioned European allies’ continued military aid to Ukraine during an unscheduled telephone call to the Coalition of the Willing summit in Berlin on Thursday, Nov. 19. According to Politico, Trump reportedly called from Air Force One, following his first trilateral summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen.

Cyberattack Hits European Commission, No Leak Found — The European Commission was hit by a major cyberattack that disrupted its internal systems for more than 10 days and may have exposed staff data, Politico reported on Thursday, Nov. 19. Hackers reportedly used ARTEX – a publicly available AI-powered tool – to identify vulnerabilities. According to the Commission’s spokesperson Thomas Regnier, no evidence has been found of a leak affecting staff. Although the attack has not been attributed to

Zelensky to Discuss Four-Way Talks With US Envoys as Europe Seeks Role — Speaking after the Coalition of the Willing summit in Berlin on Thursday, Nov. 19, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine would hold separate talks with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner on the next round of peace negotiations, which Kyiv expects to include Europe alongside the US and Russia. According to Kushner, Russia had agreed to engage in the multilateral format with European representatives.

Naftogaz Books 3 US LNG Cargoes for Early 2027 Under New Orlen Contract — Naftogaz Group and Poland’s Orlen signed a contract for three partial cargoes of US liquefied natural gas to be delivered to Ukraine in the first quarter of 2027. The gas will be regasified at the Świnoujście terminal in Poland and transported through the Polish gas transmission system. The deal follows a memorandum signed at the Carpathian Eight Summit in September 2026.

Russian Drone Damages Dutch Embassy in Kyiv — A Russian drone crashed behind the Dutch embassy in Kyiv on Thursday, Nov. 19, causing minor damage but no injuries among staff. The incident came a day after Russia’s embassy in the Netherlands publicly questioned whether The Hague was openly joining the war, with Dutch arms firm Destinus boasting of missiles used to strike the Crimean Bridge. However, there is no evidence directly linking the attack to Moscow’s rhetoric.

FACT-CHECKED: Elon Musk’s Latest Claims on Starlink, Ukraine and Russia — A Kyiv Post fact-check of Elon Musk’s DealBook Summit interview found hard echoes of Kremlin propaganda on Ukraine’s 2014 revolution, iffy claims about Starlink use in Ukraine, roughly OK Russian troop casualty figures, and a big error on Ukrainian losses.

Kyiv’s Cathedral, Foreign Embassy Damaged in Daytime Russian Strikes — Russian drone attacks damaged windows at Kyiv’s St. Volodymyr’s Cathedral and a foreign embassy, while debris fell on Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry grounds on Nov. 19. Mayor Vitali Klitschko said one person was killed and five were injured across the capital. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the ministry would put the debris in its museum.

Putin Invites Europeans to Moscow, Conditions Ukraine Talks — Russian President Vladimir Putin says Moscow has invited European representatives to discuss their position on Ukraine and European security. The proposal comes as Washington seeks to expand peace negotiations beyond the existing Ukraine-US-Russia format. Recent talks in Abu Dhabi produced an agreement on a major prisoner exchange but no significant breakthrough as Putin rejected a ceasefire in new remarks.

EU Bars Russia Residents From Erasmus+ Programs in 2027 — The European Commission’s 2027 Erasmus+ guide excludes Russia-based organizations and people living in Russia from the program, including Erasmus Mundus master’s scholarships. The restrictions apply regardless of nationality, while separate provisions cover residents of Russian-occupied Ukrainian territory. The guide, published on Wednesday, leaves unclear how the changes affect scholarships and projects approved under earlier funding cal

Kremlin Says Russia-Ukraine Prisoner Exchange in ‘Final Stages’ — Russia says a prisoner exchange with Ukraine is in its final stages of coordination and could take place soon, with intelligence services on both sides verifying the lists of prisoners. The two countries agreed in principle to the swap during US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi, and President Volodymyr Zelensky said it could return 1,200 to 1,300 prisoners of war from each side – which would be the largest exchange of the war.

Russia to Spend Record 35% of Budget on Military and Cut Social Spending — The Russian State Duma has approved a three-year budget that allocated a record 17.1 trillion rubles ($203 billion) to national defense in 2027. Military and security spending will consume 44% of federal funds, while allocations for healthcare, social support and other civilian sectors are reduced. The plan also relies on tax increases and borrowing, despite a predicted budget deficit.

Ukrainian Banks’ Profits Fall by a Third Under 50% Tax as Lawmakers Push to Extend It — Net profit of Ukraine’s solvent banks fell 33.3% year-on-year to Hr.79.7 billion ($1.8 billion) in the first nine months of 2026 under a 50% tax on bank profits, the National Bank of Ukraine said. Lawmakers are moving to extend the rate to 2027, despite warnings from the central bank and bankers that it erodes the capital banks need to keep lending.

Putin Vows ‘Far More Painful’ Response to Crimean Bridge Strikes After Talks With Trump, Xi — Russian President Vladimir Putin threatened a “far more painful” response to Ukraine’s strikes on the Crimean Bridge after three-way talks with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in Shenzhen on Thursday. He said Moscow would no longer discuss a possible partial ceasefire and promised to restore the bridge, which Ukrainian forces have hit three times in the past week, bringing down a road section.

Putin, Trump and Xi Call for UN Reform, Nuclear Dialogue in ‘Declaration on Peace’ — The US, Chinese and Russian leaders adopted a joint declaration in Shenzhen on Thursday, Nov. 19, calling for UN reform, nuclear-risk reduction and continuous energy supplies. The document also criticizes alleged abuses of jurisdiction by the International Criminal Court (ICC).

Putin Claims Russia ‘Did Not Start the War,’ Accuses Kyiv of Blocking Peace — Speaking after his trilateral meeting with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in China, Vladimir Putin claimed Russia had never started the war against Ukraine and accused Kyiv of deliberately blocking peace to avoid losing power in elections. He blamed Ukraine’s 2014 Revolution of Dignity for the conflict, omitting Russia’s occupation of Crimea, its military support for separatists in Donbas, and the February 2022 full-scale

Moscow Scrambles for Fix as Ukrainian Strikes Cripple Crimean Bridge — Moscow says it may reopen some sections within months, but Ukrainian and independent analysts question whether the bridge can be repaired while the war continues, following Kyiv’s multiple strikes on the bridge within a week, which brought down one of two adjacent supporting arches and the road that ran parallel to the railway tracks.

Kyiv Mayor Reports One Dead in Russian Drone Attack — Russian drone attacks on Kyiv left one person dead, according to preliminary information, and four injured, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said on Nov. 19. Three of the injured were hospitalized. The attacks sparked apartment fires in Podilskyi and scattered debris across several districts, following earlier damage to office buildings and a medical center.

Pentagon Official Storms Out of Ukraine Meeting After Rebuking Kyiv Over Strikes on Russia — US Undersecretary of War for Policy Elbridge Colby criticized Ukraine’s long-range strikes on Russian military and strategic targets as having little military value before leaving a NATO meeting in Brussels without hearing a classified briefing from Ukraine’s defense minister. His remarks reportedly angered European allies and fueled concerns that the Trump administration was adopting Moscow’s position o

EU Envoy Urges Ukraine to Speed Up Reforms as Russia’s War Continues — EU Ambassador Mathernová said Ukraine should regain the pace of reforms it showed in the first years of Russia’s full-scale invasion to advance its bid to join the European Union. At the forum, attended by Kyiv Post, Ukrainian anti-corruption officials called for independent wiretapping and forensic assessments, as well as broader powers for the country’s specialized anti-corruption prosecutor.

Tusk Posts ‘God, Protect Us’ After Trump Greets Putin — Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk appealed for protection from “such friends” on Thursday after US President Donald Trump warmly greeted Russian President Vladimir Putin ahead of a trilateral summit in China, though Tusk’s post did not name either leader.

From Nestor's Chronicle to Wartime Slang: Lecture Traces the Long Life of the Ukrainian Language — Language Lab is hosting a lecture on Saturday, Nov. 21 that looks at how the Ukrainian language survived centuries of bans, Russification and spelling reforms, and why it carries so much weight for Ukrainians today.

Australia Urges Putin to End War in Ukraine at APEC Summit — Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has personally urged the Russian leader to end Russia’s war against Ukraine during the APEC summit in Shenzhen. His remarks came ahead of trilateral talks between the leaders of the US, China, and Russia.

New Kerch Bridge Strikes Cause Fuel Rush in Crimea — Residents of Russian-occupied Sevastopol have rushed to buy fuel following repeated Ukrainian strikes on the Kerch Bridge, prompting occupation authorities to limit gasoline sales. Drivers can fill their tanks but are limited to 20 liters per container. The disruption adds to existing supply difficulties on the peninsula, where the bridge has served as a key transportation link with Russia.

‘Woman in White’: The Hidden Victims of Human Safari — A Russian attack drone hunted a woman in a white jacket through the streets of Kherson, and the operators posted the footage online – part of a campaign Ukrainian and international investigators call “human safari.” She survived but never appeared in any official record. Neptune Missiles Strike Crimean Bridge, ‘Symbol’ of Putin’s Rule — Ukraine’s General Staff said Neptune missiles struck the Crimean Bridge on Nov. 19, damaging its railway tracks and halting traffic. It also reported damage to three other bridges used by Russian forces in strikes on Nov. 14 and 15.

Russia Hits Odesa Region’s Energy and Industrial Sites — Russian strikes damaged energy and industrial infrastructure in the southern Odesa region overnight into Thursday, without causing casualties or disrupting power supplies, regional authorities said. The attack came a day after strikes on Odesa’s historic center killed four people. Across Ukraine, the Air Force reported 98 drones and Oniks missiles, while Moscow claimed it had also struck port facilities and a cargo ship.

Xi Urges Trump, Putin to Prevent Nuclear War — Xi urged the US, Russia, and China to prevent nuclear war and pursue disarmament, while proposing closer energy and economic cooperation. He also called for mutual respect and warned against crossing red lines, including over sensitive issues such as Taiwan.

Latvia Plans ‘De-Russification’ Declaration to Restrict Russian in Public Life — The proposed declaration would strengthen Latvian as the country’s sole official language and expand its use in public spaces, media, and workplaces. It comes amid a series of restrictions on Russian, including a ban on Russian-language content by public broadcaster LSM from January 2027.

Trump Receives Star Treatment in China as Putin’s Crimea Bridge Collapses — Putin arrived in Shenzhen after Ukrainian strikes destroyed the Crimean Bridge’s central road arch. Differences in the two leaders’ receptions complicated the image of a meeting among equals, while expectations of a grand agreement remained unfulfilled on the summit’s opening day.

Trump, Putin and Xi Concluded Three-Way Talks Without Aides in Shenzhen — Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping began talks on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen. China’s state broadcaster said the leaders would meet without aides, while the Kremlin said discussions would last no more than an hour

Ukrainian Drones Hit Key Russian Oil Hub 1,300 Kilometers From Ukraine — Ukrainian drones reportedly struck the Kaleykino oil pumping station in Tatarstan, a major hub in Russia's pipeline network, damaging oil storage tanks. Separate drone attacks were reported in Kursk, where buildings and vehicles were damaged.

Ukraine Bypassed Starlink With ‘Flying Modems’ to Coordinate Crimean Bridge Strikes — Ukrainian forces used a network of airborne relay drones to maintain live video connections with strike drones and missiles during the operation that brought down the Crimean Bridge’s 227-meter road arch. Ukrainians Embrace Dark Humour to Get Them Through Hard Times — From jokes about swimming across the Dnipro to avoid Russian drones to mock film posters and advice to stockpile 120 kilograms of sugar, a Patriot air defense system and a horse, Ukrainians are finding increasingly inventive ways to laugh through the hardship. Psychotherapist Marianna Tkalych says humour helps people regain a sense of control, maintain psychological distance from frightening events and cope with exhaustion.

Trump Sits Down With ‘Friend’ Putin Ahead of Xi Trilateral — US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin held bilateral talks in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday ahead of a three-way summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping. Trump publicly called Putin his “friend,” while Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said the Russian leader was in an “excellent mood” after the meeting. He criticizes Washington’s concessions to Moscow, warns against renegotiating European security, and urges US support for Ukraine and its European allies.

‘It Was a Mistake for Trump to Meet Putin One-on-One Without Ukraine,’ Zelensky Tells NBC — In an NBC interview, Zelensky criticizes Trump’s one-on-one talks with Putin without Kyiv, urges US-China economic pressure on Moscow, dismisses Russia’s war justification, and addresses threats against his life.

‘No Decisions Without Ukraine’: Zelensky Warns Ahead of China Summit — Zelensky stresses that Ukraine and Europe must have a say in decisions affecting their futures as Trump, Putin and Xi meet in China and Kyiv’s allies gather in Berlin to discuss military aid, financing and peace negotiations.

Putin’s Crimean Trophy Crumbles as Critics Mock His ‘Spat-On’ Arrival — Russian commentator Mark Feigin and Ukrainian journalist Vitaly Portnikov discuss the symbolic humiliation of the Crimean Bridge strikes, Putin’s weakened negotiating position, and the diplomatic victory offered by the Trump-Putin-Xi summit.

Russia Halts Train Traffic on Crimean Bridge After 3rd Strike in a Week — The Crimean Bridge came under renewed attack Wednesday, forcing Russian authorities to suspend traffic just hours before Trump, Putin, and Xi meet in China.

Council of Europe Approves €70M Ukraine Reform Plan — The Council of Europe has approved a new €70 million action plan for Ukraine covering 2027-30, aimed at strengthening democratic institutions, advancing reforms, and addressing the consequences of Russia’s war.

Witkoff, Kushner to Join Coalition of the Willing Summit in Berlin — Senior US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will reportedly attend the Coalition of the Willing summit in Berlin on Thursday, Nov. 19, Ukrinform reported, citing German government sources. The envoys are expected to meet German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, take part in the plenary session and join a press conference with President Volodymyr Zelensky. The summit, which will host nearly 40 delegations, will focus primarily on

US Arrests Alleged Russian Agent for Spying on Defense Firm Aiding Ukraine — A Russian man has been arrested in California and charged with acting as an agent of the Russian government after allegedly conducting surveillance on employees of a Silicon Valley technology and defense company that assisted Ukraine, US officials said on Wednesday, Nov. 18. Igor D’iu allegedly used physical surveillance, electronic tracking devices and fraudulent identities, and was found with $18,000 in cash and false

EU Creates Sanctions Office, Names Swedish Diplomat Danielsson as New Envoy — The European Commission set up a dedicated EU Sanctions Office on Wednesday, Nov. 18, and appointed Swedish diplomat Lars Danielsson as its next sanctions envoy, aiming to strengthen enforcement and prevent Russia from circumventing sanctions. The office is expected to cover the full sanctions cycle – from drafting to enforcement, including work with third countries – and will start formally operating on Jan. 26, 2027.

US Envoys to Debrief Kyiv on Trump’s Shenzhen Talks, Zelensky Says — US envoys are expected to brief Kyiv in Berlin on US President Donald Trump’s discussions in Shenzhen, where he is attending his first trilateral summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping, on Thursday, Nov. 19. Speaking ahead of Thursday’s Coalition of the Willing meeting in the German capital, President Volodymyr Zelensky said that decisions on Ukraine cannot be made without Kyiv’s participa

Russia Questions Dutch Role in Crimean Bridge Strike — Russia’s embassy in the Netherlands questioned on Wednesday, Nov. 18, whether The Hague was openly joining the war, after Dutch-headquartered defense company Destinus said its Ruta missiles had struck the Crimean Bridge. According to Dutch media, the company’s president said Ukraine fired nine RUTA Block 1 cruise missiles, seven of which hit the target, and called them the only foreign-made weapons in the operation. It is the first time Dest

Why the Shenzhen Summit Still Matters to the World — Three leaders. No deal expected. Why is the historic Shenzhen summit between the US, China, and Russia sending shockwaves across the globe? Find out inside.

House Republicans Threaten to Strip Ukraine Aid From Defense Bill in Oversight Dispute — Top House Republicans are seeking to strip Ukraine-related provisions from the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), including intelligence sharing, expanded military aid and sanctions on Russia. NBC News reported on Tuesday, Nov. 17, that they’re using these as leverage to force Democrats to drop measures strengthening congressional oversight of US President Donald Trump and US Defense Secretary Pete H

EU Proposes Extra €45B for Ukraine, Split Almost Evenly Between Defense, Budget — The European Commission proposed giving Ukraine an additional €45 billion in 2027, split between defense at €25 billion and the state budget at €20 billion, Finance Minister Serhiy Marchenko wrote. The money would come on top of €45 billion already planned for 2027 under the EU’s Ukraine Support Loan. Ukraine would repay the principal only after receiving reparations from Russia, and the proposal still needs the ba

Water Crisis Deepens in Occupied Crimea as Reservoir Projects Stall — Two planned reservoirs in Russian-occupied Crimea have stalled as freshwater shortages worsen, Ukraine’s military intelligence agency said. A separate pipeline to Feodosia and Kerch remains unfinished, and continued reliance on groundwater wells is making the water saltier.

Kyiv Builds Pontoon Crossings After Russian Bridge Strikes — Kyiv is building pontoon crossings over the Dnipro River to preserve essential transport links if permanent bridges are severely damaged, district head Maksym Bakhmatov said. He suggested work could finish in two to three months but expressed uncertainty about completion. Separately, bridge specialist Oleksandr Davydenko said pontoon bridges can be built in weeks, while a tunnel could take five to seven years.

Putin Brings ‘Nuclear Briefcase’ to China — An aide accompanying Vladimir Putin in China was carrying what Russian media identified as Russia’s nuclear command briefcase, APA reported on Nov. 18. Known as Cheget, the device connects the president to Russia’s nuclear command network. Similar cases have appeared alongside Putin before, including during his October 2023 visit to Beijing.

Portugal Rules Out F-16 Transfers to Ukraine, Offers Pilot Training and Aid — Portugal will not transfer F-16 fighter jets to Ukraine, citing its own air defense requirements. However, Foreign Minister Paulo Rangel says Lisbon is open to resuming pilot training and exploring ammunition supplies. The announcement comes alongside new Portuguese military funding and broader cooperation with Ukraine on drones, intelligence and defense production.

20M Russian Drones: EU Warns of Escalating Threat to Ukraine in 2027 — Russia is projected to use around 20 million drones against Ukraine in 2027, doubling estimates in 2026, EU Commissioner Kubilius said. The European Commission has proposed an additional €45 billion for Ukraine, including €25 billion for defense next year.

Ukraine Lifts Entry Ban on Mother of Savita Wagner — Ukraine lifted a three-year entry ban on Ursula Wagner after an appeal from patrol police in the Lviv region. Ursula said she had been unable to pay a speeding fine of about 6 euros during an earlier visit.

Putin Plans to Fight Through Winter Despite Talks — Western intelligence assessments indicate Vladimir Putin intends to continue the war in Ukraine at least until the end of winter, reportedly. He hopes further battlefield gains or sustained air attacks will weaken Ukrainian resistance.

Russia’s Strangulation of Ukraine’s Sunflower Oil Production Will Have Global Impact — Ukraine’s largest sunflower oil producers have suspended operations amid Russian attacks, electricity shortages, and mounting export difficulties, threatening to disrupt global supplies and push sunflower oil prices higher. Although smaller producers and alternative edible oils could partly offset the impact, Ukraine’s continued inability to export large volumes by sea poses a serious challenge to its agricult

Ukraine to Strengthen Port Security, Support Farmers for Next Sowing Season — President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine is preparing additional measures to protect Black Sea shipping and port infrastructure amid intensified Russian attacks. The plans also include cross-border security cooperation and support for farmers preparing for next year’s planting season, as export disruption threatens agricultural production.

Russia Planned Bloody Provocation in Poland to Blame Ukraine, Report Says — Russian intelligence allegedly planned a sabotage operation in Poland in late October or early November that would’ve caused heavy casualties and be blamed on Ukraine, according to Rzeczpospolita’s anonymous sources. Warsaw reinforced its border and ran drills in response. Poland’s minister-coordinator of special services did not confirm details of the plot but said the threat was assessed as real.

Ukraine Hits Bridge, Confirms 3 Russian Aircraft Damaged — Ukrainian forces struck a road bridge near occupied Stanytsia Luhanska and a military repair base in Russia’s Kursk region on Nov. 17-18, the General Staff said. It also confirmed that a separate Nov. 10 strike on the 123rd Aircraft Repair Plant damaged three Russian military transport aircraft. One Il-76 sustained very serious damage, and all three aircraft were temporarily put out of action.

Ukraine to Get World-Class Meteor Missiles for Soon-to-Arrive Gripen Fighters — Sweden and Britain will equip Ukraine’s Gripen fighters, due from early 2027, with advanced Meteor air-to-air missiles. Their ramjet propulsion and long range could give Ukrainian pilots a decisive edge over Russian aircraft, especially when paired with the Swedish-provided Saab ASC 890 AEW&C platform.

Ukraine War Accounted for Over Half of Deaths Among Russian Men in 2025 — The war in Ukraine was the leading cause of death among men ages 18 to 39 in nearly every Russian region in 2025, Bloomberg reported. A separate Financial Times analysis estimated that about 550,000 people had died in the war by August 2026.

Ukraine Urges Trump, Xi to Press Putin to End War — Ukraine expects the US and China to use their influence over Russia to help end the war when Donald Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin meet, Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said. He warned the two global leaders against giving Putin the impression of a return to an era of “spheres of influence,” and insisted no decisions concerning Ukraine could be made without Kyiv.

Russia Tests New Geran-6 Jet Drone Capable of 1,000 kph — Russia is testing a new jet-powered Geran-6 drone capable of reaching speeds of up to 1,000 kph (620 mph), Ukrainian lawmaker Fedir Venislavskiy said, citing intelligence information. The development highlights Moscow’s growing reliance on faster aerial weapons as Ukraine works to expand its air defense capabilities, including interceptor drones and electronic warfare systems.

Trump, Putin Shake Hands as Xi Hosts Summit: Bilateral Talks Planned, Kremlin Says — Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin shook hands at the APEC summit in Shenzhen on Nov. 18, hosted by Chinese leader Xi Jinping. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said a separate meeting between the US and Russian presidents is planned after the summit’s plenary session on Nov. 19. Earlier, the White House said Trump’s public schedule for Nov. 18 had ended.

Colombian Veteran of Ukraine’s Army Dies on ‘Date’ in Russian Plot — Kyiv police have detained a 19-year-old woman suspected of fatally poisoning a foreign veteran of Ukraine’s Armed Forces during a date arranged by a Russian intelligence handler. Investigators say she was promised $1,000 and filmed the victim for her handler. The case follows repeated Ukrainian warnings about Russian recruitment of young women and the use of online romance to target soldiers.

Ukraine’s Allies Pledge Missiles, F-16s at Ramstein — Ukraine’s allies outlined winter military aid at the Tuesday Ramstein meeting in Brussels. The UK announced £240 million for air defense, Germany and Norway pledged $300 million each to buy US weapons, including Patriot missiles, and Belgium reaffirmed plans to deliver 10 F-16 fighter jets by the end of 2026.

Q3 Corporate Credit Flows to Sectors Most Exposed to Russian Strikes — Agriculture, trade, manufacturing and energy – the sectors most exposed to Russian strikes on warehouses, plants and power infrastructure – supplied 94% of the third-quarter increase in hryvnia corporate loans, according to KSE Institute’s Ukraine Banking Sector Tracker. Total net lending grew a record 4.1% in August. Yet the same strikes are destroying the warehouses and plants that back the loans, leaving banks to flag coll

Russia Wants NATO Back to 1997 Borders in Exchange for Pulling Troops From Kaliningrad — Moscow has revived its demands for NATO to return to its pre-1997 positions, offering to reduce its own military presence in Kaliningrad in exchange. The proposal comes amid US-led negotiations to end Russia’s war against Ukraine, with Washington also asking Kyiv whether it would surrender Donbas in exchange for NATO membership.

5 Months On, EU Still Struggles to Bar Russian War Veterans — The EU plans to ban former Russian combatants who fought in Ukraine from entering the bloc. The proposed measures would also target around 65 shadow fleet tankers, Russian banks and cryptocurrency providers, and goods used in weapons production. First floated in April, the visa ban stalled after France and Italy objected; the European Commission is expected to present the new package for possible adoption in December.

Canada Pledges Missiles, 1.6M Rounds of Ammo in New Ukraine Package — Canada announced a new military package for Ukraine worth hundreds of millions of Canadian dollars, including funding for the Czech ammunition initiative, air defense missiles, 20 mm ammunition, surveillance systems and winter supplies. The announcement was made at the 37th Ramstein format meeting in Brussels on Wednesday, Nov. 18.

Russia Claims Nearly 90% of 2026 Recruitment Target Met but Won’t Say How Many Signed Up — Russia’s Defense Ministry says it has met 89.3% of its 2026 target for recruiting contract soldiers for its war in Ukraine but has not said how many people signed up. An independent estimate puts the number at 234,000 for January through August, a 10% drop from the same period last year.

Finland’s Stubb Urges Direct European Talks With Putin — Finnish President Alexander Stubb has urged European leaders to engage Vladimir Putin directly, criticizing their reliance on Washington to handle negotiations with Russia. He warned that US policy could favor spheres of influence and proposed six areas for talks. Stubb also insisted that decisions on Ukrainian territory belong to Kyiv and its people.

Russian Overnight Attacks Damage Austrian Honorary Consulate — Russia launched 141 attack drones against Ukraine overnight on Wednesday, Nov. 18, including 73 jet-powered drones.
